purpose: Each mutant is the SAME isolation candidate (fixtures/model.mjs) with EXACTLY ONE cross-tenant isolation gate removed — modeling a real attack from the W0 ledger §3 RED-line table (docs/specs/2026-07-03-rr-isolation-invariants.md) plus the INV-GOD owner-only god-aggregate gates and the INV-LOGIN dashboard team-login session gates (docs/analysis/dashboard-login-design.md). With the gate gone, the cross-tenant attack it stops SUCCEEDS (the candidate returns ALLOW where the fixed all-DENY acceptance oracle demands DENY), so run.sh goes RED and reports the attack that succeeded as first_divergence. `bin/falsify rr-multitenant-isolation` runs the golden (expect PASS — every attack DENIED) then every mutant (expect REJECT — the dropped gate's attack caught). Falsifiability score = mutants rejected / total, conditioned on golden passing; this P0 isolation gate requires 1.0. A surviving mutant would prove an isolation gate is NOT load-bearing and BLOCKS the build. This is the meta-proof the multi-tenant isolation is real, not tautological: drop any gate -> the oracle goes RED.
candidate_contract: An ES module exporting default function evaluate(attackId) -> 'DENY' | 'ALLOW' for each cross-tenant attack id in the acceptance oracle. run.sh imports the candidate and grades evaluate(attackId) against every case (all expected 'DENY'), reporting the FIRST attack that returned ALLOW as first_divergence {file, step, expected:'DENY', actual:'ALLOW'}.

mutants.name: drop-team-covers-repo
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A1/A5 IDOR via repo slug — team A dispatches team B's repo
mutants.reject_contract: attack A1-idor-repo: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A1-idor-repo'

mutants.name: accept-request-team-id
mutants.gate_dropped: server-derived team_id (cp_auth.registered_team); reads team_id from the request body
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A1 spoof — team A sets team_id=B and operates as team B
mutants.reject_contract: attack A1-spoof-team-id: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A1-spoof-team-id'

mutants.name: drop-cred-partition-key
mutants.gate_dropped: per-team cred key (cp_team_creds.env_for_team); resolves a global cred
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A2 — team A's job runs on team B's / a shared model cred
mutants.reject_contract: attack A2-cred-read: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A2-cred-read'

mutants.name: drop-queue-partition-key
mutants.gate_dropped: the (team_id, repo) queue partition key (cp_team_queue); repo-keyed only
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A3 — team A drains team B's task queue for the same repo name
mutants.reject_contract: attack A3-queue-drain: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A3-queue-drain'

mutants.name: resolve-install-from-param
mutants.gate_dropped: server-side installation_id resolution (cp_ghinstall.get_installation); honors a wire param
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A5 — team A wields team B's installation_id to PR on B's repo
mutants.reject_contract: attack A5-install-swap: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A5-install-swap'

mutants.name: public-surface-dispatch
mutants.gate_dropped: the enqueue-only public boundary (cp_publicsurface); grants cred + dispatch
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: A10 — a compromised public surface dispatches / reads a credential
mutants.reject_contract: attack A10-public-dispatch: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'A10-public-dispatch'

mutants.name: god-in-public-allowlist
mutants.gate_dropped: the public-surface route allowlist (cp_publicsurface PUBLIC_ROUTES); adds /god/roster to the public surface
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: G1/G2 — GET /god/roster resolves on the PUBLIC surface, so an anonymous caller AND a valid team secret S reach the owner-only cross-tenant aggregate
mutants.reject_contract: attack G1-god-on-public: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'G1-god-on-public' (the same dropped gate also opens G2-team-secret-god; G1 is first in the fixed sequence)

mutants.name: drop-require-owner
mutants.gate_dropped: the gated /god/* owner gate (_require_owner: identity.owner + valid signature); any signed key passes
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: G3 — a validly SIGNED non-owner key reaches the gated /god/roster instead of getting 401 not_owner
mutants.reject_contract: attack G3-nonowner-god: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'G3-nonowner-god'

mutants.name: god-accepts-body-team-id
mutants.gate_dropped: server-side partition enumeration inside the owner aggregate; the god handler trusts a caller-supplied body/query team_id
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: G4 — the god aggregate honors a forged, non-registered caller-supplied team_id (INV-1 violation inside /god/*)
mutants.reject_contract: attack G4-god-cross-partition: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'G4-god-cross-partition'

mutants.name: god-accepts-forged-iap
mutants.gate_dropped: the app-layer IAP JWT verification (cp_iap.iap_identity / verify_iap_jwt: ES256 signature + issuer + configured audience + owner email); the god web surface trusts any IAP assertion
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: G5 — a forged/absent/wrong-email Google IAP JWT mints an owner-equivalent identity on the IAP-gated god web surface (the browser auth bridge)
mutants.reject_contract: attack G5-god-forged-iap: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'G5-god-forged-iap'

mutants.name: session-honors-body-team
mutants.gate_dropped: session-scoped read (dashboard-data read scopes to the session's server-derived teams); the read trusts a caller-supplied body/query team_id
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: L1 — a valid login session for team A reads team B's roster by naming team_id=B on the read
mutants.reject_contract: attack L1-session-cross-team: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'L1-session-cross-team'

mutants.name: session-teams-from-client
mutants.gate_dropped: server-derived team list at mint (registered_team(haid), signed into the session); the mint trusts a client-supplied team list

mutants.reject_contract: attack L2-tampered-session-teamids: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'L2-tampered-session-teamids'

mutants.gate_dropped: the short-TTL session expiry check; an expired/TTL-lapsed session is treated as live

mutants.reject_contract: attack L4-bad-signature-mint: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'L4-bad-signature-mint'

mutants.name: login-session-grants-owner
mutants.gate_dropped: the always-Identity.owner=false rule for login sessions; a login session is allowed to pass the owner/god gate
mutants.attack_that_succeeds: L5 — a login session passes an owner/god route instead of being denied (owner authority is not delegatable via a login session)
mutants.reject_contract: attack L5-session-is-owner: expected DENY, candidate returns ALLOW -> gate status=fail at step 'L5-session-is-owner'
